proposals: PNGRB should publish terminal-by-terminal LNG regasification capacity and utilisation in an annual statistical release, instead of only in section 4.2 of a demand-projection study two fiscal years behind, so that a Dahej at 95% and five terminals near a quarter of nameplate are visible every year.

The Petroleum Planning & Analysis Cell should publish monthly LNG import volumes and landed prices by terminal alongside its national totals, so that the price-against-domestic-gas constraint this post identifies can be read terminal by terminal rather than only as an all-India average.

PNGRB should make authorisation of new or expanded regasification capacity, such as Jafrabad and the planned Dahej and Dabhol expansions, conditional on a published evacuation-pipeline and offtake plan, since Kochi and Ennore have never averaged above 13% utilisation without one.

The European Commission should publish a quarterly single-supplier concentration indicator for EU LNG imports, alongside a stated ceiling it intends to monitor against, so that the rise of the US share above 58% after Russian LNG ends in 2026 is tracked against a declared benchmark.
